tasks.short: Manage production staff and personnel concerns

steps.what: Hire, train, evaluate or discharge staff and resolve personnel grievances

tasks.design: The manager retains personnel discussions and decisions, using {HCM} for the existing records. No automated assessment, dismissal or grievance outcome is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: People decisions require context, evidence and a fair hearing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records support the manager without replacing the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving conflicting accounts and understanding individual circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: The manager listens, explains and takes responsibility for decisions.
tasks.altitude: Personnel responsibility and direct staff contact remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: the managerial personnel task remains human; no removable recruitment or record-entry baseline is inferred.

assumptions: Boundary is the production manager's personnel work, excluding separate recruitment administration and record maintenance in task 38.
The manager gathers accounts and work observations during s1; no structured performance or grievance score is assumed.
Check existing HCM configuration before custom tools; native runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new system or decision process is introduced.
unknowns: Delegated personnel authority and national procedures
research_questions: Which part of observed personnel work is conversation rather than separate administration?

already_counted.description: Personnel discussions, evaluation and decision approval

approvals.approved_version: Exact employee, supporting evidence, proposed decision and communication reviewed in s1; changed decisions require renewed manager approval and any existing higher authorisation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Scenario retains all personnel judgement and communication.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop production controls and analyse operational problems

steps.what: Develop production tracking and quality control requirements with operational data definitions
Collect operational reports and compare production and quality measures
Detect production problems and decide control-system changes from the operational comparison

tasks.design: Configure native operational reports and {BI} comparisons against the manager's tracking specification. The manager investigates data exceptions, interprets production problems and decides changes to the controls in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable measures may require repeatedly gathering separate production, quality and maintenance reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Native queries and fixed arithmetic can join existing event records when their meanings and keys are agreed.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a genuine process problem from incomplete records or a changed operating context.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands physical production and chooses workable corrective changes.
tasks.altitude: More time is available for investigating process causes; decision authority is unchanged.

reach.task: Test whether a production measure represents the actual bottleneck

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native operational comparisons can gather and calculate agreed measures; the manager still interprets problems. Savings are unmeasured scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is developing tracking controls and analysing problems; recurring official report and personnel-record preparation belongs to task 38 and is not saved twice.
In s1 the manager captures source record types and versions, site, equipment and order keys, time windows, units, metric formulas, quality categories and missing-data rules. All s1 time remains.

Operators, quality inspectors and maintenance technicians produce timestamped events, quantities, measured results and downtime reasons in the existing operational process. No new operator capture is assumed free: missing fields go to s3 for manual investigation or the proposed comparison is not deployed.

The data administrator checks source mappings before deployment and maintains them for 5 other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours. Eight additional focal hours cover changed measures and extra exceptions beyond ordinary s3 analysis.
Test native reports and BI configuration first; existing automatic collection has no human baseline and earns no saving. No machine-generated causal or quality judgement is assumed.
unknowns: Existing event completeness and common keys
Consultation needed if staff monitoring changes
research_questions: Can missing records and unit changes be found before the manager acts on a comparison?
Does report collection account for 30% of this task locally?

already_counted.description: Definition of controls and structured input contract
Data exception investigation and control decisions

incremental.description: Measure changes and additional comparison exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+0+45=70; gross 30%, minus 8 focal upkeep gives net 22%. Conservative scenarios range from existing automated reports with no new saving to 20 points of collection removed minus 8 upkeep. Definition and problem analysis keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare production reports and maintain personnel records

steps.what: Select report facts and verify production or personnel record changes
Prepare report tables or personnel record entries from verified facts
outputs: draft production report or personnel update

steps.what: Check production reports or personnel records and save the verified version
inputs: draft production report or personnel update

tasks.design: Configure templates in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HCM} to reuse verified facts for reports and record entries. The manager checks the draft, writes any explanatory text and saves the exact approved version, keeping personnel decisions separate from record copying.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts can be retyped into recurring forms and record screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field reuse and saved templates can remove copying once the manager has verified the source.
tasks.still_hard: Correcting incomplete source records and deciding the meaning of personnel or production information.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognises a technically valid entry that misrepresents what happened.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping while record accountability stays with the manager.

reach.task: Agree personnel change identifiers and correction routes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native templates can copy verified values without making personnel decisions. The proposed reduction in record-preparation time needs local measurement.

assumptions: Boundary is recurring reports and record maintenance; personnel decisions in task 36 and control-system analysis in task 40 remain separate. One report-preparation event has one owner in a team roll-up.

In s1 the manager captures report type, period, source versions, output fields, authorised destination and either production order/site/quantity/unit fields or employee ID/change type/effective date/authorisation reference. Full verification and capture time remains in the 35% share.

Operators produce original production events and authorised personnel decision-makers produce original change instructions in unchanged processes. Missing, inconsistent or unauthorised data returns to manual preparation; the system never infers an employment decision.

Native configuration is tested first; already automatic reports earn no additional labour saving. Eight extra focal hours cover template changes and unusual reconciliation, and 4 other-role hours cover record-administrator mapping maintenance.
unknowns: Actual record types and re-entry baseline
Whether existing systems already generate these reports
research_questions: Does field reuse preserve effective dates, units and source authorisation during corrections?

already_counted.description: Fact verification and structured record capture
Meaning checks, explanatory text and final record save

approvals.approved_version: Exact report or record delta, source versions, employee or production identifiers, effective period and destination checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+25=60, gross 40%, net 32% after 8 focal upkeep. Range covers already automatic records with no new gain through 23 points of copying removed minus 8 upkeep. Human verification, decisions and final checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review development plans with research and support staff

steps.what: Review plans for new products or processes
Confer with research or support staff to develop products or processes

tasks.design: The manager reviews the actual development plans in {DOCS} and discusses production feasibility with research and support staff. The design retains substantive review and collaborative development time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feasibility depends on the production setting and the proposed change.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared documents support access without replacing technical discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling development goals with practical production constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognises operational consequences and negotiates trade-offs.
tasks.altitude: Development input and decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Compare production implications of a proposed process change
reach.learn: Experimental evidence and production feasibility methods

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reviewing development plans and conferring about feasibility remain human here; a clerical summary baseline is not assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the manager's review and consultation, not drafting the development plan or running experiments.
Research or support staff supply existing plans before s1 and contribute proposals during s2. The manager creates review observations in s1; no structured feasibility verdict is assumed free.
Test native document access first. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new automation or reporting process is introduced.
research_questions: Which review decisions require direct production observations rather than plan text?

already_counted.description: Substantive plan review and development discussion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+60=100, net 0%. No summarisation saving is applied to substantive plan review or discussion.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager retains people and production decisions while native data reuse can reduce report gathering and copying.
reach: Coordinate data definitions with technicians and personnel-record owners.
role.ambitious_version: More reliable production controls and records, with time gains measured separately from staff and development judgement.
